name: Scarlet Macaw
text: The loudest colour in the canopy. Pairs fly wing to wing above the treetops at dawn, calling to each other across the mist, and they stay together for life.

name: Toco Toucan
text: That famous beak is mostly air: a light honeycomb of keratin used to pluck fruit from thin branches and to shed heat on hot afternoons.

name: Yellow-crowned Amazon
text: Green enough to vanish into the leaves until it speaks. Amazons are brilliant mimics with big personalities, and they love to sing along.

name: Sun Conures
text: Little flames of orange and gold. Sun conures travel in noisy, affectionate flocks and are never far from a friend.

name: Indian Ringneck
text: Elegant and endlessly curious, with a tail longer than its body. Males wear the dark ring around the neck, and many learn dozens of words.

name: Green-cheeked Conures
text: Small birds with enormous charm. Green-cheeks love to play, hang upside down and burrow into anything soft. Quiet for a conure, cheeky for everyone else.

name: Quaker Parrots
text: The only parrots that build stick nests: huge shared apartment blocks with a room for every family. Chatty, clever and always busy.

name: Budgerigars
text: Uma’s favourite! Wild budgies sweep across the sky in flocks of thousands, turning together like one bird. Small, bright, chattering and full of joy.

name: Lovebirds
text: Named for the way pairs sit pressed side by side, preening each other for hours. Tiny parrots with big, devoted hearts.

name: Cockatiel
text: Watch the crest: up when excited, flat when calm, half-raised when curious. Cockatiels whistle tunes, love head scratches and are gentle to the core.

name: American Barn Owl
text: As the light goes, the forest’s ghost wakes up. Its heart-shaped face funnels sound so well it can catch prey in total darkness, and its flight makes no sound at all.

name: The Waterfall
text: Every stream in the canopy finds its way here. Thank you for flying through the rainforest. This one was made for Uma.
